newsitem.title: UK: EIB aims to set trend with euro-fungible Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: EIB aims to set trend with euro-fungible Eurobond.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) wants to set benchmarks and establish a trend with Wednesday's launch of a 1.0-billion Dutch guilder euro-fungible deal, head of division capital markets Joseph Vogten told Reuters on Wednesday.
"With the deal, we hope to bring as much transparency as possible concerning the level of interest rates for the issuers in the euro Eurobond market," Vogten said.

The EIB offered a 10-year deal via ABN AMRO Hoare Govett at a yield spread of 12.5 basis points over Dutch government paper. The borrower may redenominate the deal in euros, assuming it exists, from January 1, 1999.
The spread was holding steady at 12.5 b.p. over at 1745 GMT.
"We were very happy at reaching yet another stage in the integration of markets as this should facilitate the euro," Vogten added.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett syndicate manager said institutional investors showed a warm response to the deal.

"The lion's share went to Dutch institutional investors and retail," he said. "But we saw central banks in Europe and the Far East also buy the paper as well as French institutions who were attracted by the yield pick-up."
